checks: For every t<R the chosen maximum is in the nonempty strict superlevel interval. Concavity places all indices between any two superlevel entries above t. The interval endpoints move inward as t rises, which makes κⱼ nondecreasing for the same chosen j even on a plateau. The two reciprocal denominators sum to twice the block length. The arithmetic–harmonic mean bound gives κⱼ≥1/(block length)≥1/L, and each reciprocal is at most one.

For every c<R the restriction of f−c to the strict superlevel block is concave, positive, and nonzero. Its maximum is R−c and j−a(c) is its chosen peak. At equality fᵢ=c and below the cutoff, omitted terms contribute zero because p≥2 and p−1≥1.

The map x↦x₊^p is continuously differentiable at zero for every real p≥2, with derivative zero there. Thus Qₚ′=−pQₚ₋₁, including all knots and p=2. The derivative of Qₚ(c)/(R−c)^(p+1) has the stated numerator over (R−c)^(p+2), giving the lower bound κⱼ(c)/(R−c)².

Integrating on [0,c] is valid since c<R and the lower bound is bounded and piecewise continuous there. The integral of (R−t)^(-2) on [0,c] is 1/(R−c)−1/R; after scaling this gives c(R−c)^p/R. Splitting the integral at the distinct sequence values gives exactly the stated knot sum, with no contribution from finitely many individual knots.

At c=0 the normalized bound is an equality with zero integral. The scaled integral at c<R lies between zero and c(R−c)^p/R and hence extends to zero at c=R. The other terms also vanish there. With L=1, κⱼ=1 and Qₚ(0)=R^p, so the two terms add to (R−c)^p. At every interior cutoff the simple remainder is strictly positive, proving the claimed strictness after dropping it.

Source c3c2ca0e4dcbdc9d, statement (1)–(3), proof (7)–(8), and the endpoint paragraph match the frozen assertion. Its p=1 warning is supported by the exact positive symmetric example (1/3,1,1/3) from 888842a3bcf9aa99 §3. At c=1/3, Q₁(c)=18/27 and the bound with the remainder dropped would be 20/27. At c=1/4 the values are 44/48 and 45/48, so failure also occurs away from a knot. The draft makes the scalar claim for p≥2.

overlap.comparison: On each surviving block, apply the accepted moment inequality at its exponent p−1 with N=b(t)−a(t)+1. The same derivative and integration then yield the adaptive correction with integrand 1/(N(R−t)²), and hence also the constant 1/L version. The exact chosen-peak coefficient can be strictly larger: for f=(1,1/2), R=1, j=0 and c=3/4, the peak-dependent integral is 8/3, the integral using 1/N is 5/2, and the integral with constant κⱼ(0)=2/3 is 2.

This comparison concerns a continuous affine frustum, where cap and coarea records are averaged over separately centered slope laws for integer dimension. It gives no lower bound for a uniform cutoff of an arbitrary finite concave sequence.

readability: The exact knot formula is for c<R. The statement and the proof specify that the scaled remainder has the continuous endpoint value zero at R.

summary: The derivative and integration prove the two stated lower bounds, the exact finite knot sum, and the endpoint and singleton assertions. The peak-dependent correction strengthens the count-only consequence of the accepted moment fact. Admission requires the approved frozen chosen-peak moment predecessor to be admitted first.
